Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick recap and attached materials (shortlist + prompt set + benchmark links):

Recap from demo:
- Primary workload: support ticket summarization (concise, extractive + abstractive blend) and short answer generation (single-turn, 1–3 sentences).
- SLOs: p95 latency ~200ms (preferred), throughput bursty: ~100–200 reqs/min during peak.
- Constraint: unit cost target ~10–15% below current vendor to make economics work at scale.

Attached: acme_model_shortlist.pdf (shortlist + rationale), acme_prompt_set.csv (seed prompts we used in the demo), and a link to our benchmark sheet.

Shortlist (high-level recommendation):
1) redwood-3b-quant (recommended starting point)
   - Latency: best in class on <16k context for GPU-backed hosted/dedicated (~80–150ms p95 in our internal bench on A10/40GB equiv).
   - Cost: lowest per-token cost among candidates due to quantization and small context footprint.
   - Quality: very good for summarization and targeted short answers; slightly weaker on very long-form reasoning.
   - Risk: low regression risk; we've deployed at scale for similar tasks.

2) open-llama-7b-q4
   - Latency: moderate (~120–220ms p95 depending on config).
   - Cost: mid-range; q4 quant helps reduce footprint.
   - Quality: stronger on nuanced language than 3b in some prompt families; may reduce hallucination with prompt engineering.
   - Risk: medium — should validate on your ticket set for edge cases.

3) gptx-13b-finetuned (redwood-curated variant)
   - Latency: higher (~200–350ms p95), likely requires dedicated capacity with optimized kernels to get near your SLO.
   - Cost: higher per-token but best-in-class quality for paraphrase and instruction-following.
   - Quality: highest among shortlist for nuanced summarization; fewer manual post-edits in our evals.
   - Risk: moderate-high — requires careful evals to avoid quality regressions on your domain.

Tradeoffs summary:
- If latency + cost are the priority: start with redwood-3b-quant and run a short A/B vs your current system.
- If you need higher quality on tricky language, consider open-llama-7b-q4 as a middle ground.
- If your team can tolerate higher cost/latency for best quality, run a gating eval with gptx-13b-finetuned on a small subset (~1k tickets) to measure lift vs cost.

Eval artifacts and links:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-acme-benchmarks (benchmarks + token counts + latency runs used for the shortlist).
- Prompt seeds attached: acme_prompt_set.csv (includes 50 canonical prompts for summarization + safety filters).

Next steps we recommend:
1) Agree on success criteria (quality metrics + latency targets + sample size).
2) Redwood will provision a 2-week eval on a dedicated test pool (or hosted with pinning) for the three candidate configs.
3) We’ll run automated evals + a small manual review (50 tickets) and share regression alerts.

Available times to sync and finalize the MAP next week: Tue/Thu 10–12 PT.
